newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Four killed in 3 separate Czech air crashes.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in 3 separate Czech air crashes.

text.p: Four people died and two were injured in three separate aircraft crashes in the Czech Republic on Tuesday.
Three German citizens were killed and one was injured when their light aircraft crashed on take-off near the southwest Czech town of Prachatice, a local airport official said.
Frantisek Vavruska of the Prachatice Aeroklub told Reuters that the pilot of an Aerospatiale Tobago four-seat plane and two passengers on board were killed on the spot.
The Czech news agency CTK said the third passenger suffered serious burns, but no further details were available.
Prachatice lies about 25 km (16 miles) from the Czech-German border. There were no reports of bad weather, but fog and haze on Tuesday cut visibility in patches around the country.
In a separate accident, a two-seat helicopter crashed shortly after take-off from the northeastern town of Krnov, killing the pilot, CTK reported. Further details were not yet available.
In yet another accident, a Polish AN-2 plane with a four member crew crashed into a forest close to the northern town of Liberec, slightly injuring the pilot, the agency said.
The crash apparently happened as the crew were dropping traps to catch rabid foxes near the Polish border, CTK reported.
